clue.text: Peculiar records of the people both given a spin

indicators.note: with 'given a spin', says each of the two pieces is turned round, so the first is read backwards

parts.note: EPS are extended-play records

indicators.note: something spun round faces the other way, so this word is read backwards

parts.note: laic means of the laity, the ordinary people rather than clergy

explanation.surface: Odd records belonging to ordinary folk have both been played on a turntable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both given a spin' turns each piece: EPS becomes SPE and LAIC becomes CIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Special can mean particular or distinctive to one person, which is the old sense of peculiar.

clue.text: Coin-operated "split"?

parts.note: the word split is the letter P, a ..., set inside slit, a slot

explanation.walkthrough: Put P (penny) in SLIT (a slot) and you get SPLIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Penny-in-the-slot machines work when a coin is inserted, so they are coin-operated.

clue.text: New arrangement required for end of show that may be crucial

definitions.text: New arrangement required for end of show that may be crucial

parts.words: New arrangement required for end of show that may be crucial
parts.note: the final round of the TV quiz ... is a nine-letter anagram that can decide the game

explanation.walkthrough: Countdown is a long-running British TV word and numbers game; its last round is an anagram puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: The closing anagram round of the British quiz show often settles who wins.

clue.text: Baking cake, mum's wasted a morning at army base

indicators.note: baking transforms a mixture, so these letters are reworked
something wasted is lost, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: mama is a word for mum
taken as written

explanation.surface: Baking a cake, mum frittered away a morning at the barracks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Baking' turns CAKE into ACKE; 'wasted' drops an A from MAMA to leave MMA.
explanation.definitionFit: In the old military signalling alphabet the letters A and M were spoken this way, so it is soldiers' slang for the forenoon.

clue.text: Fell on young man's digit, neglecting to drive up the wall

parts.note: Sca Fell is a fell, a mountain in the Lake District of Cumbria, England
a lad is a young man

indicators.note: neglecting a word means leaving it out of the piece

parts.note: a toe is a digit of the foot
the word is taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone fell on a lad's finger and forgot to drive the ladder up the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell' is not a past tense but Sca Fell, a Lake District peak; 'on' just joins it to what follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A scalade is an assault on a fortification by climbing its walls with ladders.

clue.text: Red 19 of X?

parts.note: X is the Greek letter chi
19 is OPPONENT; an opponent of something is anti it

explanation.surface: A red-coloured opponent of the letter X?
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a Tuscan red wine.

clue.text: Give up what requires reserve energy

parts.note: in tennis a let means the point is played again, so the server must re-serve
go means energy or drive

explanation.surface: Surrender what calls for holding back some strength.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'reserve' as re-serve: a tennis let requires the serve to be taken again.
explanation.definitionFit: To let go is to release one's hold, to relinquish something.

clue.text: Part of the Queen's Arms routine — odd item out?

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Queen's coat of arms routine with something odd left out?
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges ROUTINE plus ODD ITEM into the French motto.
explanation.definitionFit: The royal motto 'God and my right' appears on the British sovereign's coat of arms.

clue.text: 3 will be ruthless

definitions.meaning: 3 is the countdown of 3-down; a countdown will halt only at zero
to shrink from no act, however harsh

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference to 3 means only its first word, a countdown, which runs down to zero.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone prepared to do anything whatever to get their way.

clue.text: Clue, hint and key turn out charmless Rugby League team?

definitions.note: unlucky is without a lucky charm, and a Rugby League side fields thirteen players

indicators.note: turn out here suggests the letters of the listed words come out in a new order

explanation.surface: A clue, a hint and a turn of the key reveal a hapless rugby side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the letters of CLUE, HINT, KEY and TURN; 'and' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A team without luck is unlucky, and a Rugby League side numbers thirteen, giving the old superstition's phrase.

clue.text: Time taken by horribly messy method

indicators.note: a letter taken by a group of others is held inside them
something done horribly is mangled, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Time is wasted by a horribly untidy way of working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horribly' rearranges MESSY into SYSEM; 'taken by' puts T inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A system is an organised way of doing things, a procedure or scheme.

clue.text: Pence in my pockets one example of it?

definitions.text: Pence in my pockets one example of it?

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for pence in British money

indicators.note: a word that pockets another holds it inside, like a coin in a pocket

explanation.surface: A few coins jingling in my pocket might be called small spending money.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also works as a description: pocketed pence are a typical allowance of this kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Pin money is a small allowance for incidental spending, and a few pence in one's pocket is exactly that.

clue.text: Unit charged to the customer's current account?

definitions.text: Unit charged to the customer's current account?

parts.words: Unit charged to the customer's current account?
parts.note: reads like a bank charge, but the current is electric and the account is the electricity bill

explanation.walkthrough: 'current account' suggests banking; here the current is electricity, billed by the unit of power used.
explanation.definitionFit: Electricity bills charge customers per unit of energy, measured in thousands of watts over time.

clue.text: See 2
What you make during business goes to me

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in the night'
CO is the abbreviation for company, a business
taken as written

explanation.surface: Whatever you earn while working goes straight to me.
explanation.definitionFit: Income is the money one earns, so it is literally what a person makes.

clue.text: See 3
Policeman that was given to love and vigour

parts.note: the singer Sting was formerly a member of the band The Police
love is nil in tennis scoring, shown as the letter O

explanation.surface: A former police officer devoted to romance and energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Policeman that was' is not a retired constable but a former member of the rock band The Police.
explanation.definitionFit: Stingo is an old word for strength or energy, originally for strong ale.

clue.text: Inferior sofas or tables? 7 in a row

indicators.note: seven letters running together in the words, so the answer sits within them

explanation.surface: Second-rate sofas or tables, set seven to a line?
explanation.walkthrough: '7 in a row' asks for seven consecutive letters in 'sOFAS ORt'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of a sort is a poor or mediocre example of its kind.

clue.text: Choose to accept P-A-N as rival?

indicators.note: a word that accepts others takes them inside it

parts.note: to opt is to choose
the letter as printed
the letter A stands for one, as in a single item
the letter as printed

explanation.surface: Is choosing to accept the letters P-A-N enough to make you a competitor?
explanation.walkthrough: The spelt-out P-A-N looks like a word; A must instead become ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: An opponent is someone on the other side, a competitor or adversary.

clue.text: The norm to accept couples swapping halves after engagement

indicators.note: a word that accepts another takes it inside

parts.note: par is the normal standard

indicators.note: the two halves of the word change places

parts.note: twos are couples, pairs

explanation.surface: Accepted practice allows partner swapping after people get engaged.
explanation.walkthrough: An engagement is a battle, so the definition means after the fighting is over.
explanation.definitionFit: Postwar describes the period after a battle or war; engagement is a military clash.

clue.text: Remains after cremation to talk about Welsh popinjay

indicators.note: talking about something says it aloud, so this signals a sound-alike

parts.note: bone ash is what is left of a body after burning

explanation.surface: Ashes left from a funeral pyre prompt gossip about a Welsh dandy.
explanation.walkthrough: Beau Nash was a Swansea-born dandy who ruled fashionable society in 18th-century Bath.
explanation.definitionFit: Beau Nash was a famous 18th-century dandy born in Wales, and a popinjay is a vain fop.

clue.text: Extreme state

definitions.meaning: ... means total or complete, as in ... nonsense

explanation.definitionFit: Utter is both an adjective of totality and a verb of speaking aloud a declaration.

clue.text: In cycling tourists do NY state councils

indicators.note: cycling here means going round the other way, so the run is read backwards
the letters lie in the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Tourists on bicycles take in New York State.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' points to SDONYS inside 'touriSTS DO NY State'; 'cycling' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Synods are church councils or assemblies of clergy.

clue.text: See 8
Awkwardly careless telephone bidding may leave you this

definitions.text: Awkwardly careless telephone bidding may leave you this

parts.words: Awkwardly careless telephone bidding may leave you this
parts.note: careless bidding by phone at an auction can leave you with an item, a lot, you must explain

explanation.walkthrough: At an auction a lot is an item for sale; careless phone bids could land you one you must justify.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means being responsible for a great deal of trouble; here it also suggests an auction item to pay for.

clue.text: Ignorant, badly off again, say

indicators.note: taking a piece off means removing it from the word

parts.note: illiterate means unlettered or ignorant
ill means badly, as in 'ill-treated'

explanation.surface: An ignorant person is badly off once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes ILL from ILLITERATE; the definition is 'say again' with its words reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to repeat, which is to state something once more.

clue.text: Edge maintained by the head churchman

indicators.note: something maintained by another is held up inside it

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: An edge kept up by the leading clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: A primate is an archbishop, the senior bishop of a province.
